Iconoclast

/eye-KON-uh-klast/ - the stress falls on KON · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Iconoclast means one who attacks established beliefs and institutions.

The food critic made her name as an iconoclast, arguing in print that the city's most beloved steakhouse had been coasting on its legend for forty years.

Worked Example

Every September the economics faculty assigns its freshmen the same revered growth model, and every September Professor Aldana opens his first lecture by attacking it — the assumptions, the data behind it, even the fame of the man who built it. He is the department's iconoclast, and he grades hardest the essays that agree with him too easily.

Iconoclast is Greek for 'image-breaker,' and it is stronger than 'rebel': a rebel resists being told what to do, while an iconoclast turns and attacks what everyone else reveres — the sacred model, the founding legend, the untouchable rule. The word keeps its edge of demolition.

How Iconoclast Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

rebel

rebel: fights authority in any arena, often simply to resist it

dissenter

dissenter: refuses the majority view, loudly or quietly

Antonyms

traditionalist

traditionalist: defends inherited ways for their own sake

loyalist

loyalist: stands by the established order when it is challenged

How Strong Is It? — critic → dissenter → iconoclast

critic vs. iconoclast

critic vs. iconoclast: A critic finds fault and says so; that alone is far short of an iconoclast.

dissenter vs. iconoclast

dissenter vs. iconoclast: A dissenter goes further than a critic, refusing the majority view outright, but stops short of an iconoclast, who swings at the revered institution itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — icono

Root — icono: image (Greek eikon)

Root — clast

Root — clast: breaker (Greek klastes)

Put it together

Put it together: Icono (image) + clast (breaker) = image-breaker. In the eighth century, iconoclasts were believers who smashed church icons they thought were being worshipped as idols. The hammering is now figurative: a modern iconoclast swings at revered beliefs and institutions rather than at painted panels.

Use the root in a new word: icon

Use the root in a new word: icon: The trash-can icon on the desktop is a small image standing in for a whole delete program.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / pointed

Reach for iconoclast when someone does not just leave the beaten path but attacks the path itself — the revered model, the sacred tradition. A maverick (also in this unit) merely refuses to run with the herd, and heterodox describes the contrary opinions rather than the person swinging them. Iconoclast always carries the sound of something breaking.
